execution_notes.root_cause: packages/orion-research-harness/src/orion_research_harness/local_tools.py clamped every SHELL/PYTHON capability to a hard 120-second wall clock (timeout = min(max(int(payload.get('timeout', 60)), 1), 120)). The frozen QG-3 stage-1 scan of 12 candidates needs far longer than that: candidates 7-12 in the frozen order are 16-qubit Benzene DUCC batches, and a calibration probe on candidate index 6 measured 168.0 s for r6r.try_admit plus 45.1 s for r6r.stage1_predict (213.1 s total) for a single 16-qubit subject. Sibling runners (run_qg6/run_qg8_dual_harness.py) already request timeout=180 and were being silently clamped to 120 as well.
execution_notes.scientific_impact_argument: Only subprocess wall-clock ceilings changed. No scientific parameter, threshold, scan cap, gate, candidate ordering, exclusion list or predicate was altered: CANDIDATE_CAP stays 12, the R6R eligibility/order rule, the exclusion set, the DP-forbidden monkey-patch, both admission lanes' check sets and the stage-2 positive gates are byte-identical to the merged instrument. Raising the shared ceiling only permits longer timeouts; every existing caller requesting <=120s is unaffected, and the default (60s) is unchanged.

research/extensions/orion-q/max_r4d_h2o_ducc_confirmation.py: added bounded transport retry constants `_FETCH_ATTEMPTS = 4`, `_FETCH_BACKOFF_SECONDS = 3.0`, `_FETCH_NO_RETRY_STATUS = frozenset({401, 403, 407})` and a new helper `_read_source_bytes(url)` that retries only transient transport failures (HTTPError with code >= 500, URLError, TimeoutError, ConnectionError) with linear backoff, and re-raises immediately on any authorization/policy status (401/403/407) or any 4xx.

research/extensions/orion-q/max_r4d_h2o_ducc_confirmation.py: changed fetch_source's body from `with urllib.request.urlopen(SOURCE_URL, timeout=30) as r: raw = r.read()` to `raw = _read_source_bytes(SOURCE_URL)`. The following blob check (`got = git_blob_sha(raw); if got != SOURCE_BLOB: raise RuntimeError(...)`) is untouched.
execution_notes.root_cause: Outbound HTTPS in this environment goes through the session agent proxy, which was returning transient upstream gateway errors; the proxy status endpoint recorded a matching 'gateway answered 503 to CONNECT (policy denial or upstream failure)' relay failure for github.com:443 at 2026-08-21T21:00:23Z, and a direct probe of raw.githubusercontent.com returned 502 at the same time and then succeeded moments later. The frozen fetch path had no retry at all, and r6r.try_admit only catches (AssertionError, RuntimeError), so a single transient HTTPError anywhere in the twelve large library reads killed the whole scan.
execution_notes.scientific_impact_argument: The change is transport-only. Every fetched byte string still has to satisfy the unchanged git blob SHA-1 equality check against the pinned blob id before it is parsed, so a retry can only change whether a fetch succeeds, never what its content is allowed to be. Authorization and policy denials are explicitly excluded from retry, per the session proxy's guidance that 403/407 must be reported rather than retried.
